prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a coarse front-to-back layout of the workshop: the floor extends away from the camera, while the wearer’s hands and held object at the lower edge are the nearest features, roughly 0.2–0.6 m away; nearby machines, stools, and people are about 1–3 m away, and the cabinets and walls are roughly 3–6 m away. Across the five frames, bright regions show the wearer’s hands repeatedly entering arm’s reach, while people shift between the centre and right side as the camera turns; the person by the green tool cabinet remains farther away, around 2–4 m. It makes relative distance and floor geometry easier to see than RGB, including which objects occlude more distant furniture and which people are nearer than the cabinets behind them. Exact metre estimates are unreliable because the map has no metric scale, and depth around thin stool legs, hands, body boundaries, reflective machinery, and partly cropped objects is visibly smeared or inconsistent.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map separates several people from surrounding workshop objects and shows their left/right arrangement as the view changes: people appear near the lower-left, centre, and right portions of successive frames, with furniture and equipment behind or beside them. It helps expose overlap and occlusion—for example, person masks partly cover machinery or work surfaces—and shows when bodies are cut off by the top, bottom, or side boundaries; the wearer’s close hands are mostly not given useful object masks. Combined with RGB and depth, the people are approximately 1–4 m from the wearer and generally 1–3 m from one another, while labelled chairs, work surfaces, and cabinets occupy the middle and far scene; the mask alone does not reliably determine facing direction or gaze. Many labels are unreliable in this workshop context—machines and tools are called things such as car, motorcycle, suitcase, donut, laptop, or TV—and several masks are incomplete, merged with nearby objects, or absent across frames.
descriptions.pose: The pose map mainly localizes the camera wearer’s hands: magenta hand skeletons appear at the lower-left in frame 1, near the lower centre in frames 3–4, and at the lower-right in frame 5, placing them within roughly 0.2–0.7 m and showing their movement across the wearer’s field of view as the head or arms turn. It also detects a small hand-like fragment high on the right in frame 5, likely farther away and associated with another visible person, but most other people receive no usable body or hand skeletons. Where present, the finger landmarks reveal hand orientation and articulation that are difficult to resolve in the RGB strip, and they show when a hand is partly cropped or overlapping a held object. The map cannot reliably establish other people’s facing direction, gaze, inter-person distance, or reach because yellow body poses are missing and the sparse magenta detections may include false or incomplete skeletons.
